region: Villabuena de Álava · Rioja Alavesa, Spain
about: Bideona was founded in 2018, when Basque txakoli producer Gorka Izagirre bought a winery in Villabuena de Álava, in the foothills of the Sierra de Cantabria. He entrusted it to Península Viticultores, run by Masters of Wine Sam Harrop and Andreas Kubach, who set out to make Rioja that speaks of place rather than of the winery’s style. Their inheritance was remarkable: more than 300 small plots spread across Villabuena, Leza, Samaniego, Navaridas, Laguardia and Baños de Ebro, many planted in the 1920s to the 1940s.

Las Parcelas, “the plots,” sits one step above the entry-level wines in Bideona’s Burgundy-inspired range. It is Viura from small, old hilltop parcels on limestone and calcareous clay between 420 and 600 metres, bush vines averaging about 50 years old and farmed with minimal sprays. Grapes are hand-harvested into 15 kg boxes. The wine is made mostly in stainless steel and concrete, with a portion fermented in French oak barrels, used to add texture and complexity rather than oak flavour.

In the glass it is subtle at first: stone fruit, herbs and white flowers, then a juicy, poised palate with real length. Canadian critics at WineAlign were taken with the 2021, scoring it 91 to 93 points and praising its crystalline citrus, pear and wet-stone character, its taut acidity and a saline, chalky finish. Several suggested it will reward another few years in bottle.
